This Popular Car Accessory Has A Bigger Impact On MPG Than You Think

MR
By Marco Rossi Senior Supercar & Aerodynamics Editor • via Carscoops Wire
⚡ Visual Story
Source & Photography: Carscoops Wire Dispatch Verified Editorial Asset
⚡ Executive Takeaways & Key Highlights
  • Removing the roof rack crossbars from you vehicle can improve your fuel economy With fuel prices continually weighing on drivers' wallets , squeezing every possible mile out of a tank of gas is more of a priority than ever before.

In the high-stakes supercar arena, pure horsepower is no longer enough to claim supremacy. Removing the roof rack crossbars from you vehicle can improve your fuel economy

📌 The Core Development

With fuel prices continually weighing on drivers' wallets , squeezing every possible mile out of a tank of gas is more of a priority than ever before. Common fuel-saving advice includes being light-footed on the gas pedal and monitoring the tire pressure from time to time. While those steps certainly help, other factors deserve equal attention, including a popular accessory sitting directly above your head that could be quietly costing you money in the long run.

If you haven't guessed by now, we are talking about roof racks. Automakers spend millions of dollars fine-tuning vehicle aerodynamics, but practicality demands and aftermarket trends often compromise that work by significantly worsening a vehicle's drag coefficient.

🔍 Background & Sector Context

We all know that crossbars and cargo boxes are undeniably useful for longer road trips, family vacations, and camping adventures. However, if you keep driving your daily with an unused roof rack , you effectively impose a continuous tax on your efficiency.

The main issue with roof racks and pretty much any other exterior add-on is the inevitable increase in aerodynamic drag, although weight could also play its role. Roof-mounted accessories not only increase the frontal area but also interrupt the smooth airflow over the vehicle, causing turbulence.

📊 Industry & Real-World Impact

Physics taught us that these negative effects become far more pronounced at highway speeds. Meanwhile, even factory accessories with an aerodynamically optimized shape can take a heavy toll on overall efficiency.

🔮 Strategic Outlook & What Lies Ahead

A few years ago, our colleagues at Car and Driver discovered that removing the factory crossbars from their Kia Carnival press car delivered an instant improvement, bumping real-world fuel economy from 25 to 28 mpg. As a result, the minivan's highway range expanded by a full 60 miles (97 km).

In another test conducted by Consumer Reports , a Nissan Altima sedan suffered an 11% drop (5 mpg) in fuel economy at 65 mph (105 km/h) when a roof rack was installed. When combined with a roof carrier box, the efficiency toll increased to 19% (9 mpg). The effects proved to be less dramatic in a boxier SUV, but driving without a roof rack will always save you gas money.
